kicker: Paints, adhesives & tyres · crude-linked costs, Q2 FY27
title: Paint and tyre sales grew; margins fell at all 10
dek: Ten makers whose raw materials track crude grew Q2 sales 13–46% but lost margin, as price hikes lagged costs. Brent has since slipped to about $92, so Q3 shows whether the hikes now stick.

read: Pricing, not demand, is the story: buyers kept paying, but the hikes trailed costs, and a lower crude now gives them room to catch up.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Brent: NewsBytes, 17 Nov 2026
notes: Margins are operating EBITDA over revenue from operations in the filed Q2 FY27 and Q2 FY26 results, consolidated except Balkrishna (standalone), as computed by Vantage; company-reported margins can differ (Asian Paints reported a standalone PBDIT margin of about 17.1%). The ten were chosen because their main raw materials (monomers, solvents, titanium dioxide, synthetic rubber, carbon black, VAM) are crude-linked; their Q2 calls describe the same squeeze: Apollo Tyres said a ~25% raw-material rise in H1 needed 16–17% price hikes against 13–15% taken, Pidilite said VAM averaged $1,630/t vs $1,370 in Q1, and JSW Dulux said crude had come back to about $105–106 from a ~$114 peak at the time of its call. News hook: Brent traded at $91.8 on 17 Nov 2026 (NewsBytes), after falling through early November on an expected supply surplus. JK Tyre is left out because its standalone revenue rose 64.7%, so the year-ago base is not comparable; MRF has no Q2 call summary and CEAT's call data covers an earlier quarter, so their causes are not stated here. Margin recovery depends on raw material bought at older prices working through inventory, which can take a quarter.
